name: AWS Root Account Used From New Geo
description: The root account on the master payer hasn't been used in 411 days. Tonight someone logs in from an IP in a country no employee is in, opens the billing console, and creates an access key.
reasoning: AWS control plane only. CloudTrail shows the rare 'rootUser' principal used, the GeoIP is unfamiliar, and a root access key is being minted — three high-confidence signals that should each individually page.

narrative.text: Quiet baseline. Root has not been used in 411 days.
ConsoleLogin event for principal 'rootUser' from sourceIPAddress 5.34.180.x (TR).
Billing dashboard opened; spend reports downloaded.
iam:CreateAccessKey for root issued — long-lived credentials minted.
EventBridge rule 'root-login' fires; PagerDuty wakes the security director directly.
Root password reset, MFA factor swapped to a hardware key, freshly issued AK deleted.
Forensics: stolen MFA seed traced to a 2022 export from a former contractor's laptop.
Steady state. Action items: enable IAM Identity Center, kill all root keys, lock root in a vault.
